clue.text: Work for printer — me?

parts.note: the setter speaks: arranging type is the printer's job, and a crossword compiler (a setter) also sets the type of puzzle, so 'me' hints at a setter's own work

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether a printer's job description fits them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'me?' as the setter, Enigmatist, speaking: a compositor sets type for the printer, and a crossword setter is a kind of type-setter too.
explanation.definitionFit: Composing text into printable form is the printer's preparatory task of arranging type.

clue.text: Why we'll never please everybody who neatly erases goofs?

indicators.note: to goof is to blunder, so the letters of the preceding words are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tidily rubbing out mistakes is the sort who is never satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goofs' looks like the object of 'erases', but it is the anagram signal working on WHO NEATLY ERASES.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means some awkward person always objects, which is exactly why universal approval never happens.

clue.text: Erstwhile plum duffer

definitions.meaning: a dried plum, so it was formerly a plum
old slang for a silly or useless person

explanation.surface: A former plum being called a duffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Drying turns a fresh plum into this fruit, and the same word is a mild insult for a fool.

clue.text: Is this clue like an Alka-Seltzer?

definitions.text: Is this clue like an Alka-Seltzer?

parts.words: Is this clue like an Alka-Seltzer?
parts.note: a clue that can be solved and a tablet that dissolves in water share one adjective

explanation.surface: A wry question comparing a puzzle clue to a fizzing indigestion tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: Alka-Seltzer is an effervescent tablet that dissolves in water; a clue that can be worked out has the same property in its other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both capable of being dissolved and capable of being solved.

clue.text: Checker, perhaps, who won't be sticking at twenty-one

definitions.meaning: Chubby Checker popularised the dance called the Twist, so he is an example of one who twists

definitions.text: who won't be sticking at twenty-one
definitions.meaning: in the card game pontoon, also called twenty-one, a player either sticks or twists (asks for another card)

explanation.surface: Someone checking things who refuses to stop at a total of twenty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for blackjack; 'twist' is its word for taking another card, the opposite of 'stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer doing the Twist, or a card player who keeps drawing, is each one who twists.

clue.text: Where each August competitive sailors may be offensive

definitions.text: Where each August competitive sailors may be
definitions.meaning: Cowes Week, the big yachting regatta held every August, is sailed on the Solent, so racers are in the Solent

explanation.surface: Racing yachtsmen at their annual August regatta might behave badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, home of the Cowes Week regatta; the answer splits as IN SOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is rude and disrespectful, which is to say offensive.

clue.text: Broadcast desire to land and soon lose consciousness

parts.note: a programme that is broadcast is said to go out
to like is to want or desire
to alight is to land, as a bird or passenger does

explanation.surface: A pilot wants to land after a broadcast and then falls asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read GO OUT + LIKE + ALIGHT; regrouped, LIKE ALIGHT becomes LIKE A LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes falling asleep or fainting almost instantly, like a lamp switched off.

clue.text: Little girl's make-up case guards PIN, enigmatically

indicators.note: done in a puzzling way, so the letters of the preceding words are scrambled, with a nod to the setter Enigmatist

explanation.surface: A child's cosmetics case is protected by a secret PIN code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' means composition: the nursery rhyme says little girls are made of sugar and spice and all things nice.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme lists these two ingredients as what little girls are made of, so they are her composition.

clue.text: View from another wing, beneath the lower part

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed beneath another follows it

parts.note: in a piano duet the secondo is the lower part, played by the second pianist
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: An opinion from a different wing of a building, below its lower section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lower part' looks like a place, but it is the music term for the bass half of a piano duet; 'beneath' places the wing below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A further opinion is the judgement sought from another expert, such as a second doctor.

clue.text: Having variations in tune quality

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning their junction

explanation.surface: Sound quality that varies with the tune being played.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven or varying is not the same throughout, so its parts are not equal.

clue.text: Tries on pants off the shelf?

indicators.note: British slang for rubbish or poor, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper tries on trousers bought straight off the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers being tried on, but it is British slang for 'rubbish' and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods available in-store can be bought straight from the shop's display, ready-made.

clue.text: 1-1: only in second half is eleven beaten badly

definitions.note: odds of 1-1 (evens) describe a fifty-fifty wager

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are mixed up
only the back half of the word eleven is used, its last three letters

explanation.surface: A football score of one-all, with an eleven beaten only in the second half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges VEN (the back half of 'eleven') together with BEATEN. '1-1' looks like a score but is betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds of one to one mean a winning stake is doubled, the evens wager on a fifty-fifty outcome.

clue.text: Free hit to leg

indicators.note: the letters are struck and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket shot: a free hit played to the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the batter's legs side, and a free hit follows a no-ball; here 'hit' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To release or let loose is to set someone free.

clue.text: Initiates of alphabetical jigsaw and Araucaria's Xmas Club

indicators.note: initiates are beginnings, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Recalls Araucaria's famous Christmas alphabetical jigsaw puzzles, as if they had their own club.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a much-loved Guardian setter who set an alphabetical jigsaw puzzle each Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax of Amsterdam is a famous Dutch football club.

clue.text: Remember what, until her rude awakening, Goldilocks didn't have?

definitions.meaning: to keep something in mind is to remember it

definitions.text: what, until her rude awakening, Goldilocks didn't have?
definitions.meaning: Goldilocks gave no thought to the bears until they woke her

explanation.surface: Goldilocks, before the three bears woke her, had no inkling of what was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keep a fact in your thoughts, i.e. not forget it.

clue.text: Empress turned up when cross

indicators.note: turned round, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: astir means up and about
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a T-shaped cross is the tau cross

explanation.surface: An empress appears whenever she is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ASTIRAST. 'cross' looks like angry but is a T-shaped cross; 'up' looks like part of 'turned up' but is ASTIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsaritsa was the wife of a tsar, or a ruling Russian empress.

clue.text: Duke, licensed to fly, drops

parts.note: a qualified pilot has earned their wings, so owns wings

explanation.surface: A duke with a pilot's licence takes to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Downswings are falls or declines, as in a market's drops.

clue.text: Tick brown cans you need to recycle

indicators.note: recycling sends letters round, so the end of the string comes back to the front

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
tins are cans

explanation.surface: A checklist item: the brown cans have to go in the recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you need to recycle' moves the last three letters of TANTINS to the front. 'Tick' looks like a checkmark but is the British 'in a tick', a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech a tick is a very short time, a moment.

clue.text: Girl's top, simply ghastly part of uniform

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter
made horrible, the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's blouse is simply awful as part of her uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic once standard in British girls' school uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The sleeveless pinafore dress was worn by British schoolgirls as standard school dress.

clue.text: Pressure applied to a US felon

indicators.note: one piece is attached after the other

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds per (a) kilo
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Pressure put on an American criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Perp is American police slang, short for perpetrator of a crime.

clue.text: One settling on bark after wind

indicators.note: once wound round, the letters face the other way and are read backwards

parts.note: re means on or about
a yap is a sharp bark

explanation.surface: Someone resting on tree bark after a gust of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' rhymes with 'find' here: winding the letters round reverses REYAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who settles a bill or debt is the person who pays it.

clue.text: Mark's boy holding onto old record company pass

definitions.note: Mark's is read as 'Mark is', so the definition is Mark

indicators.note: the outer word grips the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
EMI was a long-established British record label
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Mark's son clings to a pass from an old record company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark, a dot over a comma, separates clauses.

clue.text: Pop's broken tea service

indicators.note: the word for tea is broken open to take the other piece inside

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
pop is short for popular, which is in; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Dad's tea service has been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like Dad but means popular, i.e. IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A china service is a set of porcelain cups, saucers and plates.

clue.text: As if this country could be construed to be Afro-Asiatic!

indicators.note: construed means interpreted, so the letters may be read in another order once the others are set aside

explanation.surface: A mock-indignant remark that a European nation could be thought Afro-Asiatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AFRO-ASIATIC are those of the country plus AS IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a Balkan country on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Misleading, as stationary ship may be?

definitions.meaning: a ship ... is held almost stationary with its head to the wind

explanation.surface: A ship standing still could be giving a false impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceiving someone by falsehood is a lie told to them; and in seamanship the phrase means heaving to.

clue.text: Dressing job performed in theatre smashes European finals

indicators.note: the operation breaks into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: two finals, each last
an op (operation) is done in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A job in the theatre crushes the European finals, needing a sticking plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashes' puts OP between the two LASTs. Elastoplast is a British brand of sticking plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking plaster is a small wound dressing.
